title: Echo Flight incident and the Boeing/SAC report
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Echo Flight incident and the Boeing/SAC report, about 1967 at Malmstrom Air Force Base, Montana, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: The reason I think that it was actually UFO related is there was a Boeing uh uh strategic air command report where they actually looked and they tried to recreate the effect and this is on the Echolight incident.
>> uh Boeing also did a bench test on what's called a logic coupler.
tellings.difference: Names the logic coupler as the part bench-tested and credits James Klotz as a source.
tellings.link_reason: Boeing's bench test of the logic coupler is the Boeing/SAC attempt to recreate the Echo Flight effect that the host describes.

tellings.quote: There's even documentation from Malmstrom's strategic air command itself, saying that they were extremely puzzled around the event and that they had no idea what was going on.

tellings.link_reason: Both tell of the 1967 Echo Flight/Malmstrom SAC documentation and Boeing's investigation into the shutdown.

as_told.title: SAC documents show puzzlement and a Boeing investigation

plain: In 1967, at Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana, a group of nuclear missiles known as Echo Flight went out of action, and some people tell this as a UFO event. A former Air Force officer, Robert Salas, appeared on a show whose title says a UFO shut down ten nuclear missiles. He says that Boeing, the company that built the missiles, ran a bench test on a part called a logic coupler to work out what happened. He credits a researcher, James Klotz, as a source for this. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it his own way. He says a report by Boeing and Strategic Air Command, the Air Force branch that ran the nuclear bombers and missiles, tried to recreate the effect. Michels says this report is why he thinks the incident really was UFO related. If the tellers are right, a company and the military tried to explain the shutdown and could not find an ordinary cause.
